subject: Proposed DPA carveout: model-insights & subprocessor visibility — signoff request
messages:
From: Legal Ops <contracts@brightwellhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Sujata Rao <sujata@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redline proposal: model insights carveout

Hi Avery —

Attached is Brightwell's proposed redline to the DPA. The change we care most about is an explicit carveout for "model insights": analytics derived from model behavior (e.g., aggregate prompt patterns, embedding statistics, and anonymized usage telemetry) that we share with our analytics partner to improve product integrations. Our counsel added language to exempt model insights from certain restrictions so we can continue to work with our analytics subprocessors.

High level: we are not asking for training rights or raw transcript sharing. The redline removes limits on sharing aggregated metrics and derived embeddings used for integration tuning.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is acceptable under your security posture? If not, please propose alternative language — Brightwell needs a clear path before legal will sign the MSAs by month-end.

Attachments: brightwell_dpa_redline_v3.pdf

—
Sujata Rao
Head of Legal Ops
Brightwell Health

Subject: Re: DPA redline proposal: model insights carveout

Sujata / Brightwell team —

Thanks for the redline and the clear framing. Looping in Product and Product Security so we can get an internal decision and a suggested counterproposal. A few immediate clarifying questions from Sales/Product: 

1) Can you confirm the intended granularity of "model insights"? (aggregate metrics only, or per-session embeddings?)
2) Will any third-party subprocessors receive token-level telemetry or only aggregated summaries?
3) Is Brightwell expecting retention > 90 days for these artifacts?

We'll review and come back with a short set of allowable constraints. For context, this carveout potentially touches telemetry export, subprocessor allowlists, and model-output visibility — all areas Product and Security need to sign off on. I've uploaded a redline diff we use internally here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDLINE_DIFF (internal).

Ask: Olga / Priyom / Marcus — can you weigh in on acceptable limits (examples below) and flag any blockers: 

- Allow aggregated metrics (e.g., counts, latency histograms, embedding distribution summaries) to subprocessors, but prohibit raw transcripts and prompt + response pairs.
- Allow embeddings sharing only if pseudonymized and scoped to a hashed customer id, and with retention capped at 30 days unless explicitly approved.
- Require subprocessors to be on our allowlist and pass a SOC2-type review; model artifacts must be encrypted at rest.

If we can agree to one of these patterns I will propose it back to Brightwell.

Thanks —
Avery

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: DPA redline proposal: model insights carveout

Avery / team —

Quick security summary after a first pass on Brightwell's redline: we cannot accept an unconstrained carveout that permits sharing of per-session embeddings or any unredacted outputs that could be used to reconstruct user content. Specific concerns and proposed mitigations below: 

Concerns: 
- Per-session embeddings + context may enable re-identification or leakage of PHI when combined with other datasets.
- Token-level telemetry or full prompts/responses should never be exported to third-party subprocessors without explicit legal/customer opt-in.

Proposed guardrails (minimal viable set): 
1) No raw prompt/response export. Exports must be pre-aggregated or summarized; no per-session vectors unless hashed and salted with a customer-scoped secret.
2) Embeddings allowed only as aggregated statistical deltas (e.g., centroid vectors for cohorts), or as pseudonymized vectors tied to a customer-scoped hashed id (no PI).
3) Retention default: 30 days for telemetry/embeddings. Any longer retention requires documented business justification + Security & Legal signoff.
4) Subprocessor access: must be on Redwood's allowlist; require an executed DPA between Redwood and the subprocessor or proof of equivalent controls (SOC2 Type II / ISO27001).
5) Auditing: require export logs surfaced to the customer and to Redwood's Console for periodic review.

Operational impact notes for Product: these constraints may require changes to our export service (masking layer + allowlist enforcement) and will add ~2 sprints of work for the telemetry/exports team if Brightwell insists on per-customer hashed vectors. Marcus / Priyom — please confirm capacity and UX implications.

—
Olga Petrov
Senior Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Dec 2028 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redline proposal: model insights carveout — signoff request

Team / Brightwell —

Thanks Olga — that layout helps. Priyom / Marcus, please confirm which of the three paths below Product can accept and an estimated ETA to implement guardrails if Brightwell will not narrow their ask: 

Option A (Preferred, lowest risk): Aggregated-only metrics allowed. No embeddings exported. Implementation: no infra changes; Product signals export level via flags.
Option B (Compromise): Pseudonymized embeddings allowed with default 30-day retention and allowlist enforcement. Implementation: requires masking + allowlist work; estimated 2 sprints and a cross-team rollout (Product + Telemetry + Security).
Option C (High-risk): Per-session embeddings shared with Brightwell subprocessors under broad retention >90 days. Not recommended by Security; Legal would need to draft strong indemnities and carveouts.

Next steps: 
- Priyom / Marcus: reply with which option Product would sign off on and an implementation ETA. If Product wants Option B or C, provide a short list of required infra tasks and whether a pilot is possible.
- Olga: if you agree with Option A/B framing, confirm security wording we should propose back to Brightwell.
- Legal: I will push a short counterproposal to Brightwell within 24 hours after Product + Security pick an option.

Deadline: Brightwell has asked for a path to signature by month-end. Can we lock this by EOD Thursday (2028-12-13 PST)? If that's tight, call out blockers now.

Attachments: internal_playbook_model_telemetry.md (internal summary of telemetry guardrails). HubSpot deal: hubspot://deal/BW-ENT-4921
